scope: All 30 selected candidates; only rewritten retained excerpts are source-checked. Publisher claims were compared, not independently audited underlying datasets.

entries.retained_excerpt: The Real Deal reported that April 2025 searches on the MIAMI Realtors portal were led by China (13%), followed by Colombia (9%), Venezuela (7.7%), Canada (7.4%) and India (5.2%). Search interest is not completed purchases.
entries.findings: Corrected third-through-fifth country rankings. Removed unsupported currency, outbound-investment, visa and buyer-preference explanations. Publisher text was available through its indexed article result after direct access failed.
entries.checked_title: China unseats Colombia as top foreign country searching for Miami homes

entries.findings: Supplied URL could not be retrieved. Its title matches the subtitle of article 01; that article supports only a subset of this digest’s detailed claims. Excluded pending a correct distinct source or a deliberate merge.
Publisher preview confirms title and May 29 date but does not expose the body. Cannot verify numbers or the flagged 2025 U.S. election reference. Remains quarantined.
Publisher page confirms title and May 30 date, but the scorecard is an image and its detailed numerical contents were not verified. Narrative explanations are not supported by the visible page text.
Supplied Sun Sentinel URL could not be retrieved. No claim-level verification of the cited page was possible.
Supplied Newsweek URL could not be retrieved; cancellation rates and quoted explanations remain unverified.

entries.retained_excerpt: MIAMI Realtors reported year-to-date time on market of 62 days for Miami-Dade condos in buildings aged 30+ years, versus 79 days for those aged 29 years or less. Separately, June 2025 condo sales at $1 million and above rose 6.4% year over year; the June existing-condo median rose 6% to $450,000.
entries.findings: Corrected reporting scope: the 62/79-day comparison is year-to-date, not June alone. Did not label it a median because the text does not. Removed additional unchecked inventory claims.
entries.checked_title: Miami-Dade Older Condominiums Selling Faster than Newer Units; $1M & Up Condo Sales Continue Rising

entries.retained_excerpt: MIAMI Realtors reported Palm Beach County year-to-date residential dollar volume of $11.7 billion, up 1.84% from a year earlier. June 2025 median prices fell 5.2% to $626,000 for single-family homes and 3.1% to $315,000 for existing condos. June total dollar volume fell 7.16% to $1.8 billion.
entries.findings: Retained checked prices and distinguished year-to-date growth from June dollar-volume decline. Omitted cash share, supply and causal explanations from this excerpt.
entries.checked_title: Palm Beach County Year-to-Date Total Dollar Volume Higher Than Last Year

entries.retained_excerpt: MIAMI Realtors reported June 2025 Miami-Dade median sales prices up 2% year over year to $670,000 for single-family homes and up 6% for condos/townhomes. Its analysis described a fourteenth year of appreciation despite lower sales across Southeast Florida counties in the first half of 2025.
entries.findings: Retained the article’s historical comparison without claiming every condo month rose uninterrupted. Removed unchecked county shares and explanations.
entries.checked_title: 14 Consecutive Years of Home Price Appreciation for Miami Real Estate

entries.findings: Supplied Newsweek URL could not be retrieved; statewide sales and price figures remain unverified.

entries.retained_excerpt: SFGATE carried a Realtor.com midyear forecast projecting 2025 existing-home sales of 4 million, down 1.5%, and national home-price growth of 2.5%. These were forecasts published in July 2025, not realized results.
entries.findings: Retained forecast values; removed the delisting causal claim and percentage from this excerpt. No later outcome is implied.
entries.checked_title: Home Sales May Fall to New 30-Year Low in 2025 as Mortgage Rates Remain Elevated

entries.retained_excerpt: Real Estate Market & Lifestyle reported May 2025 Palm Beach luxury new contracts up 10.5% year over year for single-family homes and 5.1% for condos. It contrasted this with declines exceeding 45% in Miami-Dade contracts and reported Broward new listings in the $1 million–$3 million segment up 58.4%.
entries.findings: Core digest figures match the linked article. Kept May reporting distinct from July publication and avoided extrapolating the segment to all properties.
entries.checked_title: Palm Beach lidera auge inmobiliario de lujo en Florida (Palm Beach Leads Luxury Real Estate Boom in Florida)

entries.findings: Direct publisher access returned a JavaScript verification challenge. Contract counts, asking volume and listing inventory remain unverified.
Supplied El Nuevo Herald URL could not be retrieved. Project claims and inferred effects on for-sale demand remain unverified.

entries.retained_excerpt: In a September 7, 2025 commentary, The Real Deal described price reductions, longer selling times and greater condo choice in parts of South Florida. Citing Redfin, it reported more than 21% of July pending purchases canceled in Fort Lauderdale and about 17% in Miami. These are historical observations and attributed data, not a current market assessment.
entries.findings: Retained attribution and restored “more than 21%.” Removed unsupported buyer-sentiment and demand-discount explanations. Publisher article body was available in its indexed result after direct access showed a JavaScript challenge.
entries.checked_title: The Weekly Dirt: Signs of a buyer’s market in Miami

entries.findings: Direct publisher access returned a JavaScript verification challenge. Pipeline size, branded projects and presale percentages remain unverified.
Supplied publisher URL could not be retrieved. Indexed promotion confirms the title only, not the detailed summary.
Fox Business fetch was restricted. The July primary article independently supports a narrower time-on-market comparison, but this source’s full explanation was not verified.
Publisher preview confirms September 4 date and a housing-market topic, but the body was unavailable. The title shown differs from the digest. Numeric claims remain unverified.

entries.retained_excerpt: A MIAMI Realtors release on PR Newswire reported September 2025 Miami-Dade total residential sales of 1,769, up 4.6% year over year. Transactions at $1 million and above rose 19.9%, from 296 to 355. The release described September as the strongest sales month of 2025 to that point.
entries.findings: Retained checked counts and period; omitted unreviewed affordable-condo and median-price claims from this excerpt.
entries.checked_title: Miami-Dade Real Estate Registers Best Sales Month of the Year; Affordable and $1M & Up Condo Transactions Surge

entries.retained_excerpt: MIAMI Realtors reported Palm Beach County September 2025 total home sales up 21.6% year over year, from 1,628 to 1,980. It reported a 51.3% all-cash share and $1 million-and-above transactions up 20.92%, from 282 to 341.
entries.findings: Removed the digest’s unsupported claim that Palm Beach had the highest national cash ratio; the article’s national ranking refers to Miami, a different geography. Omitted other unchecked figures.
entries.checked_title: Palm Beach County's Top-Ranked All-Cash Market Shielded from Elevated Mortgage Rates

entries.findings: Direct publisher access returned a JavaScript verification challenge. County articles corroborate some individual sales changes, but this article’s combined dollar-volume claims remain unverified.

entries.retained_excerpt: MIAMI Realtors reported Broward September 2025 residential sales up 9.2% year over year, from 1,850 to 2,021. Transactions at $1 million and above rose 26.59%, from 173 to 219. It described September as Broward’s strongest sales month of 2025 to that point.
entries.findings: Retained checked counts and comparison; omitted other unchecked prices and growth figures from the excerpt.
entries.checked_title: Broward County Real Estate Posts Best Sales Month of the Year

entries.findings: Publisher URL redirects to Content Expired. The original rate figure, date and causal explanation could not be checked.

entries.retained_excerpt: Zillow’s October 20, 2025 release described September activity as unusually resilient for the season. Of the 50 largest U.S. metros, 15 were classified as buyer’s markets, compared with six a year earlier. Miami was among the strongest buyer’s markets. National inventory was up 14% year over year, while pending sales fell 5.4% from August.
entries.findings: Repaired the obsolete investor-site URL using the matching publisher release. Retained historical month and national versus metro scope.
entries.checked_title: Lower mortgage rates extend housing momentum into fall

entries.retained_excerpt: National Mortgage Professional, citing Redfin, reported that 25.3% of U.S. homes sold above final list price in September 2025. The average sale-to-list ratio was 98.6%, equivalent to 1.4% below final asking price. These measures reached their lowest September levels in six years.
entries.findings: Corrected seasonal scope: lowest September levels, not an unqualified six-year low. Removed unrelated regional figures from the retained excerpt.
entries.checked_title: Homebuyers Benefitting From A Sluggish Market

entries.retained_excerpt: South Florida Agent Magazine reported that China and Singapore ranked first and second in September 2025 web searches for South Florida real estate, followed by Colombia. The report concerns online interest, not completed purchases or proven future investment.
entries.findings: Kept the supported search ranking. Removed policy, legal-status and residency-program speculation rather than presenting it as investment guidance.
entries.checked_title: China and Singapore lead web searches for South Florida real estate

entries.retained_excerpt: Diario Las Américas reported that PropertyShark’s 2025 ranking placed Fisher Island ZIP code 33109 first nationally, with a $9.5 million median sale price, up 65% from the prior year. This is a historical ranking reported in October 2025.
entries.findings: Corrected publication date from October 17 to October 18, 2025; the former appears in an image filename. Kept digest period separate.
entries.checked_title: Fisher Island, el código postal más caro de EEUU en 2025 (Fisher Island, the most expensive ZIP code in the USA in 2025)

entries.retained_excerpt: Commercial Observer reported a proposed 30-story Calta Group project at 1415 Northwest 13th Terrace in Miami’s Health District: 499 apartments and 14,696 square feet of commercial space. The proposal designated 40% of units for people earning 120% of area median income under the Live Local Act. This was a September 2025 proposal, not a completed development.
entries.findings: Corrected apartments versus condos. The article does not support the name Anatomia, 210 workforce units, 299 condos, or a mid-2026 groundbreaking; those claims were removed.
entries.checked_title: Calta Plans Residential Tower in Miami’s Health District Using Live Local Act

entries.findings: Redirected publisher page displays December 31, 2025, conflicting with the digest’s September date. Original version unresolved.
